# Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Worth Weighing


By:[Paul Dykewicz](https://www.dividendinvestor.com/author/pdykewicz-admin/)


, September 4, 2026


Link copied!


Three dividend-paying container investments worth weighing for potential purchase have gained buoyancy as the Strait of Hormuz conflict continues.


The three container investments include two tanker companies that focus on shipping oil, along with an exchange traded fund that holds a variety of shipping stocks and offers a dividend yield above 5%. Both container stocks have advanced for much of 2026, spurred by an unusually robust crude tanker market, market analysts reported.


Reasons for the share price gains include positive corporate earnings reports and market updates, a confluence of geopolitical disruptions, trade route adjustments and historic supply constraints that caused rate increases for their customers in 2026.


**Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Worth Weighing: Carlson’s Counsel**


Even thought Iran roiled global energy markets, energy prices have not increased as much as most analysts expected despite restricted shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, said Bob Carlson, who heads the *[Retirement Watch](http://www.retirementwatch.com/offer/rw-default/?source=GURURW1)* investment newsletter and is the creator of a proprietary[IRA calculator](https://www.retirementwatch.com/offer/rw-ira-calculator-v2?source=GURURWCALCV2) for those considering Roth IRAs conversions.


The price of a barrel of Brent crude oil rose from about $61 at the end of 2025 to a peak of over $127 in April, said Carlson, a retired pension fund chairman who makes investment recommendations for *[Retirement Watch](http://www.retirementwatch.com/offer/rw-default/?source=GURURW1)* subscribers and gives them weekly updates about the markets and analysis about topics that pertain to retirees and pre-retirees. But the Brent crude oil price dropped sharply to around $68 in July and recently traded between $90 and $100, he added.


“When the Strait of Hormuz was first closed, many energy analysts talked about expectations of $150 per barrel,” Carlson continued. “One reason the $150 level has not been reached is that the major players in the energy markets adapted to the change of circumstances with impressive speed and flexibility. But investors and consumers need to be aware that we could be approaching the limits of these workarounds.”


*[Bob Carlson](https://www.retirementwatch.com/about-bob-carlson/) meets with[Paul Dykewicz](https://holysmokesbook.com/contact-us) .*


Even though the world went into the conflict with significant surpluses of oil in both ships and storage tanks, much of the stored oil has been released, Carlson counseled. For example, the U.S. Strategic Petroleum Reserve is reported to be near its lowest level since 1982.


In addition, Middle East reserves also are near targeted or required minimums, while China reduced its purchases in global markets during the conflict partly because it stored significant, though unknown, quantities of oil and established its own refineries, Carlson continued. Energy analysts predict China soon will be unwilling to further reduce its reserves and will increase its purchases, he added.

*Bob Carlson is a former pension fund chairman.*


**Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Worth Weighing:** **SB**


Safe Bulkers Inc. (NYSE: SB), of Monaco, operates dry bulk cargo vessels across the world, providing marine dry bulk transportation services for goods such as coal, grain and iron ore, along shipping routes across the world. Shipping rates have surged since the U.S.-Iran military conflict erupted. With the normal transit far from reality right now in the Strait of Hormuz, Wall Street and U.S. Army veteran Jim Woods is forecasting no end in sight to this situation.


Woods recently recommended Safe Bulkers to subscribers of his[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) advisory service. SB is not only moving higher on strong technical indicators and bullish “NewsQ,” but it also satisfies his fundamental criteria with robust sales growth, profit margins, earnings-per-share growth, price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and institutional buying, he added.


“I suspect these bullish drivers to continue,” wrote Woods, who leads the[TNT Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tnt-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUTNT) ,[Tactical Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/tactical-trader-web-default-offer/?source=GURUTT01) *,*[Five Star Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/five-star-trader-web-default-2/?source=GURUFST) and[Bullseye Stock Trader](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/bullseye-default/?source=GURUBEST1) advisory services that recommend both stocks and options.


*Jim Woods is rated as the No. 1 stock blogger by Tip Ranks.*


“In line with our financial performance in the second quarter of 2026, which was supported by a relative strong charter market, we increased our quarterly dividend to $7.5 cents per share,” said Dr. Loukas Barmparis, president of Safe Bulkers, when the company reported second-quarter 2026 results on July 28. “The basic components of our policies, which include a strong balance sheet, liquidity and capital resources, conservative leverage and fleet renewal with newbuilds replacing older tonnage, reflect our ability to operate a continuously upgraded, modern fleet with improved competitive characteristics.”


That means we have the financial resources to invest when required, and reward our shareholders, Barmparis continued.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


Woods, who also heads the[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) investment newsletter, recently helped his subscribers by recommending non-dividend-paying Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF (AMEX + BATS: BWET) in late July and then advising to take profits of 62.36% in slightly more than four weeks.


Money always goes to where it’s treated best, Woods wrote when recommending the fund in late July. That proposition is one where veracity nearly always applies, he added.


**Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Worth Considering: Woods’ Wisdom**


The Breakwave Tanker Shipping ETF was recommended in the[Forecasts & Strategies](https://jimwoodsinvesting.stockinvestor.com/offer/fs-web-default-2/?source=GURUFS) ‘ Tactical Trends Portfolio by Woods, who predicted that the conflict in Iran is not close to ending, neither in terms of future bombing and operational action, nor in the effects it is having on the key waterway chokepoints such as the Strait of Hormuz, and now the Bab el-Mandeb strait.


Brent crude oil recently started to rise again, as a potential second front in the military conflict with Iran has opened in the Bab el-Mandeb strait, Woods continued. The Bab el-Mandeb is on the western/other side of the Arabian Peninsula, opposite of the Strait of Hormuz, so it is not nearly as important as the Strait of Hormuz during normal times, but these are not normal times, he added.


Advertisement.


A specialized exchange-traded fund, BWET tracks the cost of shipping crude oil via wet freight futures contracts rather than investing in standard shipping company stocks. Since the U.S./Iran military action started, Saudi Arabia has been sending oil that normally would be exported through the Strait of Hormuz to the port city of Yanbu. From there, the oil is loaded onto ships and sent mostly to Asia via the Bab el-Mandeb strait, Woods wrote.


Prior to the war, Saudi Arabia exported about 1 million barrels per day (bpd) from Yanbu but, after the war started, boosted it to nearly 5 million bpd, offering an important workaround for the reduced Hormuz transit, Woods advised his subscribers.


**Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Show Buoyancy: STNG**


Monaco-based Scorpio Tankers Inc. (NYSE: STNG) is an international tanker shipping company founded in July 2009 to transport refined petroleum products. Scorpio Tankers has pulled back significantly in recent months but is showing signs of climbing again.


BofA Global Research downgraded STNG’s shares to underperform from Buy in late June and reduced its price objective on the stock to $78 from $100. The share price closed at $80.11 on Sept. 3, up from $79.61 at its close on Tuesday, Sept. 1. The stock continued inching up by trading at $80.75 shortly after the market opened on Sept. 4.


The now-escalating military conflict between the United States and Iran could aid the share price of STNG. BofA reduced its outlook when progress was starting to occur earlier in the summer with peace negotiations and a memorandum of understanding (MOU) between the United States and Iran.


BofA increased its 2026 and 2027 EPS estimates 62% and 16%, to $16.90 and $6.10, from $10.40 and $5.25, respectively, according to a research note in late June. The investment firm forecast improved profitability for the company despite reducing its rating on the stock.


Scorpio Tankers should continue to drive significant free cash flow in the near term given those extended rates, BofA wrote.

**Three Dividend-paying Container Investments Include an ETF: BOAT**


“Shipping containers have always been a very cyclical business,” said[Michelle Connell](https://www.portia-capital-management.com/michelle-connell) , founder and chief investment officer of Dallas-based[Portia Capital Management](https://www.portia-capital-management.com/why-portia-capital) . “The market is either flooded with them during economic booms or there are shortages during recessions.”


*Michelle Connell heads Dallas-based Portia Capital.*


Advertisement.


Connell continued that she discovered it professionally during the subprime mortgage crisis that occurred primarily during the mid-2000s and culminated in an economic downturn by 2007 that extended into 2010.


“I worked for a Chicago private equity firm that had ties to Sam Zell, the famous real estate investor,” Connell counseled. “The CEO of our firm and Sam Zell, along with our industrial analyst, traveled along the Mississippi to find mothballed shipping containers. They managed to purchase many at highly discounted prices and ended up selling them at a great profit once the economy turned around.”


Due to the ongoing conflict in the Strait of Hormuz, the number of shipping containers has fallen and become highly sought after, Connell told me. Now is good time for investing in these assets and benefiting from the income streams that they produce, she added.


An efficient way to invest in this asset class is through the SonicShares Global Shipping ETF (NYSEARCA: BOAT), Connell said. The fund’s top three holdings are Mitsui O.S.L Lines, Ltd. (TYO: 9104); Kawasaki Kiensen Kaisha, Ltd. (TYO: 9107) and SITC International Holdings Co, Ltd. (HKG: 1308).


Income investors may appreciate BOAT’s current dividend yield is 5.56%.


*Chart courtesy of[www.stockcharts.com](http://www.stockcharts.com/) .*


**Investments to Buy During the Strait of Hormuz Conflict: Geopolitics**


With fresh military action taking place in the Strait of Hormuz and Ukraine, global geopolitical risk remains a big concern, and these three investments offer a potentially profitable path forward to receive income and share-price appreciation amid the chaos.
